newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus-Waigel adamant on '97 German deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Focus-Waigel adamant on '97 German deficit goal.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he would hold to his planned budget deficit goal next year, despite the release of new forecasts showing tax revenues would be lower than expected in 1996 and 1997.
"We will stick to planned new borrowing of 56.5 billion marks ($37.40 billion) in 1997," Waigel said in a statement after the publication of the tax estimates.

An independent working panel said 1997 total tax revenues, at 822.2 billion marks, would be 10.3 billion marks down on its last forecast in May, while 1996 revenues would be five billion marks lower at 805 billion marks.
Federal revenues in 1997 are seen five billion marks below earlier expectations at 344.9 billion marks. This year's inflow was revised down three billion marks to 340.6 billion marks.

Waigel, who is determined to make Germany qualify under the strict criteria for European monetary union, said the revisions for 1997 were already covered by savings in the government's Programme for More Jobs and Growth drafted last spring.
Further savings of seven billion marks have been included in the 1997 draft budget, but Waigel said he was still seeking cuts of three billion marks in spending next year.

A cabinet meeting on Friday reached broad agreement on the cuts, which will be submitted by the three coalition parties and finally agreed on late on Sunday. A final 1997 budget draft will be put to parliament's budget committee next week.

Waigel's deficit target refers to the federal budget, over which he has direct responsibility. But he has no direct control over regional and local authorities, and appealed to them to match his savings efforts to ensure that Germany meets the Maastricht treaty's three percent deficit limit.
"The federal government will, despite lower tax revenues, hold firm to the essential goal of reducing the defict. States and communes must equally meet their responsibility to save," he said.
"We must jointly ensure that the preconditions on the way to investment, jobs and European Economic and Monetary Union are established," he said.
